findings.title: Persistent USE failure loops forever with no bound or transient/permanent distinction
findings.claim: When the keyspace is dropped or USE is rejected repeatedly, every new connection fails USE and is discarded, so the pool stays empty and republishes Broken(UseKeyspaceError) each time; nothing bounds this or distinguishes permanent from transient errors, and there's no test for repeated failures.

findings.title: No shard-aware fallback to regular port after a keyspace failure
findings.claim: When requested_shard is set, the Keyspace branch does not fall back to the regular port and does not remove the shard-aware attempt, so USE failures on an already-open shard-aware connection slow refilling (via had_error_since_last_refill backoff) unlike connect failures on that port.

findings.title: Test still polls with sleep loop despite 'avoid busy-waiting' commit title
findings.claim: full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics loops with sleep(1ms) on get_total_connections() inside a 5s timeout; despite the commit being titled 'avoid busy-waiting', this is still polling and can be flaky under load.

findings.title: PR description omits unrelated metric-balance changes
findings.claim: Most of the metric-balance changes (decrement_total_connections in maybe_reshard and at both excess-clear sites, plus three new tests) are not part of the keyspace fix and are not mentioned in the description, though they appear correct.
